newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Nat.Australia Bank says Irish/UK profit off.
newsitem.headline: Nat.Australia Bank says Irish/UK profit off.

text.p: National Australia Bank, parent of National Irish Bank, said on Thursday that operating profit for its UK/Irish banking and financial operation dropped in Australian dollar terms although was higher in local currency terms in 1995/6.
It said operating profit, before amortisation of goodwill, of the UK/Irish banking and financial services group fell by 4.0 percent to $403 million.
NAB said the UK/Irish divisions profits dropped as a result of higher provisions for bad and doubtful debts and a stronger Australian dollar.
But in local currency terms operating profit rose 2.6 percent compared with the previous year, NAB said.
National Irish Bank is due to release results for the year later on Thursday morning.
NAB said good growth in lending was achieved in personal and business markets but cost to income ratios were lower in all four regional banks in the UK and Republic of Ireland.
NAB reported operating profit for the group of $2,102 million for the year to September 30, 1996, a 6.8 percent increase on the previous year.
